svg.aria-label: A cloud agent run — bounded, brokered, and finished by a human
svg.title: A cloud agent run — bounded, brokered, and finished by a human

g.text: A cloud agent run — bounded, brokered, and finished by a human
Step Functions is the run state machine (CREATED → … → COMPLETED). Tools go through a policy broker; the result is a patch proposal the desktop commits.
1 · The author starts a skill: POST /v1/agent-runs with skill id, scopes, budgets and an idempotency key.
2 · The starter validates the skill manifest; skill prose can never widen permissions.
3 · It loads grants (principal + action + scope + expiry). Anything not granted is denied.
4 · Without a hosted index, the desktop uploads a context pack: only in-scope documents, deleted when the run ends.
5 · StartExecution is named by the idempotency key, so a retry never starts a second run.
6 · Planner and writer steps call Bedrock; the budget is checked before each call.
7 · The run reads only its context pack (or the consented hosted index).
8 · Every tool call goes through the broker: schema, grant, quota and timeout.
9 · Code tools run as a Fargate task: isolated subnet, no internet, CPU/memory/time caps.
10 · MCP tools go through an adapter that enforces a destination allowlist.
11 · Tool results come back tagged untrusted and are sanitized before the model sees them.
12 · The draft becomes a patch proposal: diff, base revision, evidence and a provenance label per paragraph.
13 · The run waits on a task token; 'approval required' is pushed to the desktop over WebSocket.
14 · The author approves the exact patch hash; the desktop commits it with compare-and-swap and reindexes.
15 · The committed revision resumes the run (SendTaskSuccess). Reject or timeout ends it as REJECTED or EXPIRED.
16 · The outcome, grants used, tools called and sources read are appended to the audit log.
